policy_summary:
Overnight camping is prohibited at ALL Conwy car parks. The council does provide designated campervan and motorhome bays at Morfa Bach in Conwy and space at Maelgwyn Road in Llandudno, but these are larger DAYTIME bays - no hook-up, no waste disposal, and no overnight stays. Campervans may also use other car parks without height barriers, parked wholly within the markings.

This puts Conwy at the restrictive end of the north Wales spectrum: provision for the vehicle, none for staying in it. Gwynedd, Anglesey and Denbighshire are all expanding overnight provision; Conwy is not.
notes: CORRECTED. An earlier version of this record, taken from a third-party motorhome directory, claimed designated overnight bays at Betws-y-Coed at GBP5 for 24 hours. The council's own page contradicts that flatly. A good argument for reaching authority sources before publishing anything.
open_questions: What instrument backs the prohibition - an off-street parking order, or policy?
Are there on-street restrictions as well?
Which car parks have height barriers? The council mentions them without listing them.

sites.name: Morfa Bach Car Park, Conwy
sites.notes: Designated campervan and motorhome bays, sized for larger vehicles. DAYTIME ONLY - overnight camping is prohibited here as everywhere else in Conwy. Useful if you want to visit Conwy in a van, useless if you want to sleep in it.

sites.name: Maelgwyn Road Car Park, Llandudno
sites.notes: Council describes it as having suitable space for campervans and motorhomes. Daytime only.

sites.name: All Conwy County Borough car parks
sites.notes: Council wording: overnight camping is prohibited at all our car parks. Blanket, county-wide, with no designated exception anywhere.
